# Sumedhātherīgāthā (Thig 16.1)

**ID:** Thig 16.1
**Section:** Therīgāthā (thig)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Sumedhātherīgāthā
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/thig16.1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0509m.mul15.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sumedhātherīgāthā* (Thig 16.1) is a text within the *Therīgāthā* of the Pali Canon, consisting of an exceptionally long set of seventy-five verses attributed to the nun (*therī*) Sumedhā [Collett 2014; SuttaCentral]. It forms one of the longest individual compositions in the collection, preserving an extensive biographical narrative [Collett 2014]. SuttaCentral records eleven modern translations across eight languages, including English versions by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

A related canonical account of her life is found in the *Sumedhātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 1), although the narrative traditions in the *Therīgāthā* verses and the *Apadāna* biography diverge significantly [Collett 2014; SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal overlap, including 53 matches with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and three verses directly shared with the *Sumedhātherīapadāna* (specifically Thig 16.1 §70.4–72.2 aligning with Thi-Ap 1 §2.1–4.2) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects machine-generated alignments with various Mahāyāna and Āgama texts, notably the Sanskrit *Yogācārabhūmi*, the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99), and Tibetan translations of the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna*, the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, and the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* [DharmaNexus].
